SMTO-FIL-0017 — SMTO expected a file but found a folder

GUID: f27cf265-8eb3-4faa-ab7e-b3dee4265a94
Slug: file-not-a-file
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO tried to treat a folder as a single file, for example to read it, save over it, or copy it without saying to include its contents. It stopped at that step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you want to copy a whole folder with everything in it, tell SMTO clearly to copy the folder and all of its contents. Copying a whole folder has to be asked for on purpose; otherwise SMTO only copies single files.
  2. If you meant one file inside that folder, tell SMTO the file's full name and location. Naming the file lets SMTO open the file rather than the folder around it.
  3. If SMTO was saving a file, check that no folder in that place already has the same name. A file can't be saved over a folder with the same name.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads, saves or copies the item you meant and the step finishes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. For a saved Run, don't swap in a different file or folder without deciding that on purpose.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation that requires a regular file got a directory: the OS returned EISDIR, or file.copy received a directory source without recursive=true.

What this means

  • The OS reported a directory where a file was required, or copy received a directory without recursive mode. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The OS reported a directory where a file was required, or copy received a directory without recursive mode.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect resource type and the operation's recursive flag; do not infer a corrupt file.

How to fix it

  • Check path_context in the receipt. Point content operations at a regular file, or call file.copy with recursive=true when copying a whole directory tree is intended (gateway_core/file_manage.copy, file_common.error_kind).
  • Select a regular file or use the operation appropriate for a directory.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A regular-file operation or deliberately authorized recursive copy matches the resource type.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
